Spoty 0.1.0 is the first release: a tiny native Spotify player for Windows. It's a single 5 MB exe that uses about 30 MB of RAM and no CPU while idle. It plays your music through Spotify Soloist, Spotify's own lightweight player, which Spoty downloads and keeps up to date for you.

**Download Spoty:** [Windows (x64)](https://github.com/ladroxd/spoty/releases/download/v0.1.0/spoty.exe) · [SHA-256 checksum](https://github.com/ladroxd/spoty/releases/download/v0.1.0/spoty.exe.sha256)

No installer: download `spoty.exe` and run it. Windows may show a SmartScreen warning because the app isn't code-signed; click **More info → Run anyway**. You need Spotify Premium and a free [Soloist API key](https://developer.spotify.com/dashboard/soloist); Spoty walks you through both on first launch.

## New

- **Your whole library.** Search, Liked Songs, playlists, saved albums and followed artists, with album and playlist covers.
- **Find things fast.** Filter the sidebar by name, show only playlists **by you** or **by others**, and right-click to **pin** playlists, albums and artists to the top.
- **Playback controls.** Play, pause, seek, next and previous, shuffle, repeat (all songs or this song) and volume. Space toggles play and pause.
- **Lives in the tray.** The close button keeps Spoty playing in the tray; right-click the tray icon to quit. Optionally start with Windows.
- **One window only.** Opening Spoty a second time switches to the one that's already running.
- **Preferences.** Name shown in Spotify, starting volume and audio cache limit, plus a button to clear the cache.
- **Light on your PC.** The UI is drawn on the CPU, so no browser engine or GPU driver is loaded; covers load only for what's on screen and are capped at about 1.5 MB.

## Good to know

- The first time, pick **Spoty** once in the Spotify app's device list (on your phone or another computer) to link the player to your account.
- Playlists that use Spotify's 4-album mosaic cover show a placeholder instead.
- Spoty isn't made or endorsed by Spotify.
